items.text: Sensitive assets, entry points, service identities, privileged operations, and trust boundaries have named owners and current data classifications.
Privileged and high-impact actions require strong authentication with a phishing-resistant option, and account recovery is tested to the same assurance level.
The server denies by default and validates the current identity, action, tenant, resource, and context on every sensitive request.
Inputs are parsed against bounded schemas, database operations are parameterized, outputs are contextually encoded, and file content is constrained and scanned.
Sessions use protected transport and cookie settings, rotate when privilege changes, expire within a documented window, and can be revoked promptly.
Secrets are stored outside source code, workloads receive least-privilege identities, and encryption keys are separated, versioned, rotated, and access-logged.
Security events capture actor, action, resource, outcome, policy version, time, and correlation ID without recording passwords, tokens, keys, or sensitive bodies.
High-risk alerts have an owner, bounded response objective, escalation route, and a recent end-to-end test from event creation through acknowledgement.
Identity, API, export, upload, and expensive query boundaries have tested rate, size, concurrency, and cost limits with explicit client behavior.
Policy, identity, key, event, and scanning dependency failures have documented fail-closed or bounded-degradation behavior; none silently become an allow.
The team has measured token and key revocation, workload isolation, evidence preservation, clean restore, data reconciliation, and customer communication.
Dependencies, images, infrastructure, and configuration are scanned, findings are triaged by reachability and impact, and remediation deadlines have accountable owners.
